description: INNER, LEFT, RIGHT — connect two tables and control which rows survive.

questions.code:
SELECT students.name, enrollments.course
FROM students
INNER JOIN enrollments
  ON students.id = enrollments.student_id;
questions.explanation: Five enrollment rows have matching students: Morolake x2, Tega, Ama, Priya.
questions.prompt: How many rows does this return?

questions.code:
SELECT students.name, enrollments.course
FROM students
JOIN enrollments
  ON students.id = enrollments.id;
questions.explanation: enrollments has no id column — the match must use enrollments.student_id.
options: The ON clause uses enrollments.id, which doesn't exist — it should be enrollments.student_id

questions.prompt: Arrange these lines into a valid query.

questions.code:
SELECT s.name
FROM students AS s
___ enrollments AS e
  ON s.id = e.student_id;
questions.explanation: LEFT JOIN keeps every left-table row, NULLs for misses.
questions.prompt: Keep every student, even without enrollments.

questions.explanation: The join type decides which rows survive; ON decides how they connect.
